questions.question: When riding motorcycles in a group, should you use a staggered formation?

options.text: No, not when entering or leaving a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, not when entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is good for group riding, but switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What is the key to making a quick turn on a motorcycle?

options.text: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn, you need to lean your motorcycle in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are required to wear proper eye protection.

questions.question: If you are towing a trailer on a motorcycle, how should your following distance change?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase it.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The trailer adds weight, so your motorcycle will need more time to stop.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Where you can see and be seen best.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can see and be seen best.
questions.explanation: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle to see oncoming traffic early and let other drivers see you. On a left curve, ride on the right side of your lane. On a right curve, ride on the left-center of your lane.

questions.question: What formation should a group of motorcyclists use when taking a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What should you do with your brakes when making a U-turn?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike.
Use the front brake for stability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the motorcycle to tip over. Use only the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following you too closely.
When you will be slowing down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as noticeable as car brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping suddenly so other drivers will notice you are decelerating.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, ride slower and allow more stopping distance. The passenger should hold onto the motorcycle's passenger handholds or the operator's waist, hips, or midsection—not just the back of the bike.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: In broad daylight.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in broad daylight. Always wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: What should you do to control a motorcycle well?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly when holding the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from danger, push gently on the handgrip on the side where you want to go.

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated when their blood alcohol content (BAC) is ____ or higher.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Do not drive a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both front and rear brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases their visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you best. Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster. Slow down at intersections. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move into the portion of the lane that will bring you into another driver's field of vision as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal and then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the portion of the lane that will bring you into another driver's field of vision as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Move into the part of the lane that other drivers can see you in as early as possible.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look downward to see the changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up in work zones. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the posted speed limit to complete the pass, but not by more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: Complete all passes within legal speed limits. Pass only when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: In general, which lane position is best to ride in?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Adjust your position as conditions change.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn. Do not turn your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn. Do not turn your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders may cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: If passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may go faster than the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may pass in a no passing zone if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes within the posted speed limit. You may only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, ride in which part of the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left part of your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles will enter the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, ride in which part of the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of the lane is safest. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too early, which is also dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have room to steer.
You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react quickly and steer away from danger. It does not give you more time to speed up in curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same direction. Solid white lines mean do not pass. Dashed white lines mean you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles move slower than 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.
